description:
# Epic — model/provider/codex realignment with pi-mono

## goal

Bring zi's model catalog, provider registry, and resolution chain into structural parity with pi-mono so that:

1. The catalog encodes the **auth-method duality matrix** (same model id served under multiple `(provider, api, base_url)` tuples — one per auth pathway).
2. Initial-model resolution follows pi-mono's exact ladder (`findInitialModel`), with as little hardcoded provider-specific knowledge in `main.zig` as possible.
3. zi's first-launch supports three providers, each with both api-key and (where applicable) subscription auth:
   - **anthropic** (api key + claude-code subscription via shared provider key — no catalog duplication needed, AuthStorage handles it)
   - **openai** (api key) + **openai-codex** (chatgpt PKCE subscription — distinct catalog rows because base_url and api differ)
   - **openrouter** (api key)
4. Custom models can be defined in `~/.config/.zi/settings.json` via a `models[]` array, mirroring how pi-mono users add e.g. fireworks-kimi.

## architecture decision (locked)

```
┌─ process const ───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ src/ai/models_generated.zig                                   │
│   pub const models = [_]Model{...}   ← comptime, 325 rows     │
│ src/ai/defaults.zig                                            │
│   pub const default_model_per_provider = [_]Entry{...}        │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
┌─ per-session, agent-owned ────────────────────────────────────┐
│ src/ai/model_registry.zig                                     │
│   ModelRegistry {                                             │
│       allocator,                                              │
│       models: []const Model,    ← built-ins ++ custom         │
│       custom_backing: []Model,  ← owned copies                │
│       auth: *AuthStorage,       ← borrowed                    │
│   }                                                           │
│ owned by AgentSession.                                        │
│                                                               │
│ Bundle (provider_defaults.zig) STAYS UNTOUCHED — its scope    │
│ is "provider transport runtime", not "model discovery".       │
│ Growing it would blur concerns. Per oracle finding (see       │
│ "Oracle insights" below).                                     │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
            ┌───────────────┴──────────────┐
            ▼                              ▼
┌─ agent thread ─────────┐     ┌─ tui thread ──────────────────┐
│ resolve.findInitialModel│     │ binds []const Model slice    │
│ resolve.restoreFromSession   │ from registry.getAll() at init│
│ set_model handler validates  │ reads AuthStorage.hasAuth()   │
│   patterns via resolve       │   directly (already           │
│ streamFn picks model from    │   mutex-protected, doctrine-  │
│   AssistantMessage           │   sanctioned cross-thread     │
│                              │   shared service)             │
│ ModelRegistry on AgentSession│ NEVER calls                   │
│                              │   ca.model_registry.*         │
└──────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────────┘
```

## phase ordering

| phase | issue | depends on |
|---|---|---|
| 1a | catalog port (anthropic+openai+openai-codex+openrouter) | — |
| 2  | ModelRegistry + defaults.zig + resolve.zig (port model-resolver.ts) | 1a |
| 3  | Register openai-responses + openai-codex-responses + openai-completions providers in Bundle | 2 |
| 4  | OpenAI Codex PKCE oauth flow + auth.json storage + openai_codex provider | 3 |
| 5  | Custom models via settings.json `models[]` (the fireworks-kimi-style use case) | 2 |

Phase 1a is **already shipped**. This epic tracks phases 2-5 and serves as the canonical context dump.

## status as of phase 1a

- catalog: 325 models (22 anthropic, 41 openai, 9 openai_codex, 253 openrouter)
- `gpt-5.4` correctly appears twice: once `.openai` / `api.openai.com`, once `.openai_codex` / `chatgpt.com/backend-api`
- only `anthropic-messages` is registered in `Bundle.init` (provider_defaults.zig:56). openai/openrouter/codex have NO stream implementation yet — phase 3 work.
- `main.zig:resolveModel` (lines 444-475) and `default_models_per_provider` (479-503) reference models for stripped providers (groq/cerebras/xai/google/etc.). Resolution silently falls through to step 4. Phase 2 deletes both and replaces with `resolve.findInitialModel`.

## oracle insights (locked design rationale)

### why ModelRegistry is session-owned, not process-global, not in Bundle

> **Oracle finding (verified)**: Settings are cwd-scoped (`src/settings/manager.zig:15-17`, `manager.zig:35-38`, `main.zig:312-319`). `SettingsManager.create(...)` takes `cwd`. The full catalog (built-ins + custom models) is therefore NOT process-global even though built-ins are. Process-global lazy singleton is the wrong shape.

> **Oracle finding (verified)**: `provider_defaults.Bundle` is documented as "canonical built-in provider bundle" — provider transport runtime (`provider_defaults.zig:1-18`). It exists because entry paths were hand-building provider registries. It owns provider structs + `Registry` for `AgentSession` teardown. Growing it to also own model resolution blurs "provider transport" with "model discovery/selection". Don't overload it; if a unified runtime container is wanted, make a new concept.

> **Oracle finding (verified)**: pi-mono creates `ModelRegistry` from `AuthStorage` as a normal runtime object, not a singleton (`.references/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-registry.ts:262-275`). zi's `AgentSession.Options` already carries per-session runtime deps like `auth_storage`, `session_store`, `registry` (`src/coding_agent.zig:81-107`). Session-owned matches both pi-mono and zi lifetime boundaries.

### why TUI does NOT reach into agent-owned ModelRegistry

> **Oracle finding (verified)**: AGENTS.md threading doctrine (lines 67, 90-93, 112-113):
> - agent-owned registries/tools are read by TUI via published snapshots (line 67)
> - snapshot rule: "TUI needs to read data to render or filter. Agent publishes an immutable frozen value" (lines 90-93)
> - anti-pattern: "Reaching across for 'just a read'" (lines 112-113)
>
> Therefore: if ModelRegistry lives on AgentSession, TUI must NOT call `ca.model_registry.*` directly.

> **Oracle finding (verified)**: `AuthStorage` is already an explicit cross-thread shared service with its own mutex (`src/auth/storage.zig:21-44`, `282-293`). `hasAuth()` is mutex-protected and only checks availability. TUI already stores `*AuthStorage` and filters the model picker with `hasAuth()` (`interactive.zig:180`, `1122-1144`). Login worker mutates auth storage directly on success (`interactive.zig:1356-1358`). For live auth availability, **direct TUI reads via `AuthStorage.hasAuth()` are sanctioned**.

### resulting v1 access pattern

- TUI binds `model_catalog: []const Model` once at init from `registry.getAll()`. Catalog is immutable for the session's lifetime in v1 (no hot-reload), so the slice pointer stays valid.
- TUI calls `auth_storage.hasAuth(provider_string)` directly for live availability checks in the model picker.
- Agent thread is the only one that calls `registry.find/findExact/getAvailable/hasConfiguredAuth`.
- Mutations (model switch) flow through `AgentRequest.set_model` as today. Validation happens on the agent thread inside the handler, calling `resolve.resolveCliModel`.

### what we explicitly do NOT need in v1

- An `available_models` snapshot published via `event_queue` — only needed if picker should auto-refresh availability without reopening after `/login`. Out of scope for v1; reopen-after-login is fine.
- Hot reload of custom models — settings are read at session init, period.
- Async `getAvailable` — pi-mono's is async because of OAuth refresh. zi's `hasAuth()` is sync and lock-protected; we keep it sync.

## pi-mono reference files (read these BEFORE implementing any sub-issue)

All paths relative to `.references/pi-mono/`:

- `packages/ai/scripts/generate-models.ts` — full TS generator (1590 lines). Phase 1a ports lines 60-655 (provider fetches), 657-739 (cost/context patches), 720-917 (additions block), 941-1056 (codex hand-coded block), 1496-1517 (dedup logic).
- `packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts` — the 629-line file that phase 2 ports verbatim. Functions: `defaultModelPerProvider` (lines 14-38), `findExactModelReferenceMatch` (64-106), `isAlias` (50-57), `tryMatchModel` (112-142), `parseModelPattern` (180-233), `resolveCliModel` (328-458), `findInitialModel` (474-554), `restoreModelFromSession` (559-628), `buildFallbackModel` (151-165), `ScopedModel` / `ResolveCliModelResult` / `ParsedModelResult` / `InitialModelResult` types.
- `packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-registry.ts` — the ModelRegistry phase 2 mirrors structurally.
- `packages/coding-agent/src/core/sdk.ts` — how pi-mono wires ModelRegistry into the session.
- `packages/coding-agent/test/model-resolver.test.ts` — golden test cases for parseModelPattern, etc. Use as fixture source for phase 2 tests.
- `packages/ai/src/openai-codex.ts` (or wherever codex provider lives — phase 4 will trace it) — the PKCE oauth implementation.

## doctrine reminders (must follow)

From AGENTS.md:

- **Don't approximate the protocol.** Find the exact pi-mono function before writing zig. Trace every event, field, and ordering.
- **Don't port the syntax.** No line-by-line ts→zig translation. `async/await` → blocking, `Promise.all` → sequential, `.map()` → loops, `try/catch` → error unions or result fields.
- **JSON serialization**: NEVER hand-roll. Use `std.json.Stringify` for writing (`jw.objectField("camelCase")` for snake→camel mapping), `std.json.parseFromSlice` for reading. camelCase wire format, snake_case zig fields.
- **Shared utils**: `src/ai/json_util.zig` for `cloneJsonValue`, enum↔string converters (`providerToString`, `parseProvider`, `parseApi`, etc.). Use these instead of local copies.
- **Threading**: ModelRegistry is agent-owned. TUI reads `[]const Model` slice + `AuthStorage.hasAuth()` directly. Mutations through `AgentRequest`. Adding new cross-thread paths requires the four-step protocol from AGENTS.md §"Adding a new cross-thread action".
- **Testing doctrine**: max 3-5 tests per task. Test behavior at boundaries, not function-by-function. Conformance fixtures from pi-mono (run pi-mono's tests, capture outputs).
- **Build**: `zig build` is the compilation gate. Do NOT run `zig build test` (times out). Use `zig test src/file.zig` for standalone tests.

## DAG

```
zi-epic (this issue)
├── phase-2: ModelRegistry + resolve.zig + defaults.zig
│   └── blocks phase-3, phase-5
├── phase-3: register openai/openai-codex/openrouter providers
│   └── blocks phase-4
├── phase-4: codex PKCE oauth flow
└── phase-5: custom models via settings.json
```

phase 5 only depends on phase 2 (the ModelRegistry seam). it does NOT need phase 3 or 4 because custom models reuse existing registered apis.

description:
# Phase 2 — ModelRegistry + defaults.zig + resolve.zig (port model-resolver.ts)

## context

Read the parent epic first for the full picture, oracle insights, and doctrine reminders. This issue is the implementation spec for phase 2.

After phase 1a, the catalog has 325 models across 4 providers, but `main.zig:resolveModel` (lines 444-475) is a 30-line shim that doesn't match pi-mono's `findInitialModel` (629 lines of resolution logic). Phase 2 deletes the shim and ports `model-resolver.ts` faithfully, threading a session-owned `ModelRegistry` through.

## scope

3 new files, 4 modified files. ~600 lines of new zig + ~50 lines of deletions.

### NEW: `src/ai/defaults.zig` (~25 lines)

Mirrors pi-mono `model-resolver.ts:14-38`. Declaration order = priority. Phase 1 set:

```zig
const protocol = @import("protocol.zig");

pub const Entry = struct {
    provider: protocol.Provider,
    id: []const u8,
};

/// Default model id per provider, walked in declaration order during
/// findInitialModel step 4 (first authed provider's default model).
/// pi-mono source: packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts:14-38
pub const default_model_per_provider = [_]Entry{
    .{ .provider = .anthropic,    .id = "claude-opus-4-6" },
    .{ .provider = .openai,       .id = "gpt-5.4" },
    .{ .provider = .openai_codex, .id = "gpt-5.4" },
    .{ .provider = .openrouter,   .id = "openai/gpt-5.1-codex" },
};
```

Verify all four ids exist in `models_generated.zig` before committing. They should — the patch block in phase 1a added them.

### NEW: `src/ai/model_registry.zig` (~150 lines)

Read-only snapshot, session-owned, immutable for the session lifetime. Built once at session init from `models_generated.models ++ settings.custom_models`. Holds a borrowed `*AuthStorage`.

```zig
pub const ModelRegistry = struct {
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    /// Merged catalog: built-ins first, then custom models from settings.
    /// Const slice into either generated.models directly (when no custom
    /// models) or into custom_backing (when there are).
    models: []const protocol.Model,
    /// Owned heap copies of custom models. nil when there are none, in
    /// which case `models` aliases generated.models directly.
    custom_backing: ?[]protocol.Model = null,
    /// Borrowed — caller owns lifetime.
    auth: *auth_storage.AuthStorage,

    pub fn init(
        allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
        auth: *auth_storage.AuthStorage,
        custom_models: []const protocol.Model,
    ) !ModelRegistry { ... }

    pub fn deinit(self: *ModelRegistry) void { ... }

    /// All models, built-ins + custom, in declaration order.
    /// pi-mono: ModelRegistry.getAll()
    pub fn getAll(self: *const ModelRegistry) []const protocol.Model;

    /// Find by exact (provider, id) match.
    /// pi-mono: ModelRegistry.find(provider, id)
    pub fn find(self: *const ModelRegistry, provider: protocol.Provider, id: []const u8) ?protocol.Model;

    /// True if AuthStorage has credentials for this model's provider.
    /// pi-mono: ModelRegistry.hasConfiguredAuth(model)
    pub fn hasConfiguredAuth(self: *const ModelRegistry, model: protocol.Model) bool;

    /// Filtered slice of models that have configured auth. Caller owns
    /// the returned slice. Sync (zi's hasAuth is sync, unlike pi-mono).
    /// pi-mono: ModelRegistry.getAvailable() — but ours is sync.
    pub fn getAvailable(
        self: *const ModelRegistry,
        allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    ) ![]protocol.Model;
};
```

#### invariants to enforce

- `getAll()` returns a stable slice for the session's lifetime. Never mutate.
- `models` slice MUST contain all entries from `generated.models` first, custom_models appended. Never reorder. This matches pi-mono's "first registered wins" precedence — built-ins win over user customs on collision.
- `hasConfiguredAuth` calls `auth.hasAuth(json_util.providerToString(model.provider))`. The string conversion is the contract — must round-trip with `parseProvider`.
- For phase 2, `custom_models` is ALWAYS empty (`&.{}`). Phase 5 wires it to settings. Don't try to plumb settings through yet.

#### testing

Three tests max:

1. `test "registry returns all built-in models when custom is empty"` — verifies `getAll().len == generated.models.len` and the slice equals `generated.models[..]`.
2. `test "find by provider+id matches anthropic claude-opus-4-6"` — round-trip a known catalog entry.
3. `test "hasConfiguredAuth delegates to AuthStorage.hasAuth"` — use a mock AuthStorage that records the lookup string and asserts it equals `"anthropic"`.

### NEW: `src/ai/resolve.zig` (~400 lines, the bulk)

**1:1 port of `model-resolver.ts:1-629`.** Read the full pi-mono file before writing a single line. Trace every branch. The behavior must match pi-mono exactly so existing pi-mono session files and CLI usage transfer.

#### types to port

```zig
pub const ScopedModel = struct {
    model: protocol.Model,
    /// nil = use default; phase 2 always nil since --scope isn't wired
    thinking_level: ?protocol.ThinkingLevel = null,
};

pub const ParsedModelResult = struct {
    model: ?protocol.Model,
    thinking_level: ?protocol.ThinkingLevel,
    warning: ?[]const u8,
};

pub const ResolveCliModelResult = struct {
    model: ?protocol.Model,
    thinking_level: ?protocol.ThinkingLevel,
    warning: ?[]const u8,
    /// non-null + model=null means CLI should print and exit non-zero
    err: ?[]const u8,
};

pub const InitialModelResult = struct {
    model: ?protocol.Model,
    thinking_level: protocol.ThinkingLevel, // never null; defaults to DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL
    fallback_message: ?[]const u8,
};
```

Strings in result structs are arena-allocated by the caller-provided allocator. Document this clearly.

#### functions to port

In dependency order. Each one cites its pi-mono source line range.

1. **`isAlias(id: []const u8) bool`** — pi-mono lines 50-57. Returns true if id ends with `-latest` or does NOT match `-YYYYMMDD$` regex. Implement the date check as a manual byte scan (no regex stdlib). 8 chars trailing must all be ASCII digits AND preceded by `-`.

2. **`findExactModelReferenceMatch(reference, available_models) ?Model`** — pi-mono lines 64-106. Three-stage match:
   - Stage 1: case-insensitive `provider/id` canonical form match. If exactly 1 hit, return. If >1, return null (ambiguous).
   - Stage 2: if reference contains `/`, split on first `/` and try `(provider, id)` exact pair. If exactly 1, return. If >1, null.
   - Stage 3: case-insensitive bare-id match across all providers. If exactly 1, return. Else null.
   - Use `std.ascii.eqlIgnoreCase` for case-insensitive comparisons.

3. **`tryMatchModel(pattern, available_models) ?Model`** — pi-mono lines 112-142. Calls `findExactModelReferenceMatch` first; if no hit, falls back to substring match against `id` and `name`. Then splits matches into aliases vs dated, prefers aliases sorted high-to-low, else dated sorted high-to-low. The sort is pi-mono's `localeCompare(b.id, a.id)` — port as `std.mem.lessThan(u8, b.id, a.id)` reversed (i.e. descending byte-wise).

4. **`isValidThinkingLevel(s) bool`** — helper. Matches pi-mono `cli/args.ts:isValidThinkingLevel`. Returns true if s is one of `"minimal" | "low" | "medium" | "high" | "xhigh"`. Map to `protocol.ThinkingLevel`.

5. **`parseModelPattern(pattern, available_models, opts) ParsedModelResult`** — pi-mono lines 180-233. Recursive descent:
   - Try `tryMatchModel(pattern)` first; if hit, return with thinking_level=null.
   - Else find last `:`. No colon → return all-null.
   - Suffix after colon valid thinking level → recurse on prefix; if recursion found a model AND no warning, attach this thinking_level. If recursion warned, drop thinking_level.
   - Suffix invalid: if `allow_invalid_thinking_level_fallback=false`, return all-null. Else recurse on prefix and if found, attach a warning string.
   - The recursion is depth-bounded by pattern length / colon count; safe.

6. **`buildFallbackModel(provider, model_id, available_models) ?Model`** — pi-mono lines 151-165. Used by `resolveCliModel` when an explicit `--provider` is set but the `--model` doesn't match anything in that provider. Picks the first model with `model.provider == provider` whose id matches `default_model_per_provider[provider]` (or first if no default), clones it, and overrides `id` and `name`. The returned model is a fresh struct value — no allocation needed since `Model` is value-typed.

7. **`resolveCliModel(opts) ResolveCliModelResult`** — pi-mono lines 328-458. The big one. Logic:
   - If `cliModel` empty → return all-null.
   - Get `availableModels = registry.getAll()` (note: `getAll`, NOT `getAvailable` — phase 2 detail to preserve, lets `--api-key` work for first-time setup; pi-mono comment lines 339-340).
   - Build provider map (lower → canonical) from available models.
   - If `cliProvider` given but unknown → error.
   - If no provider given, try to interpret `provider/model` from cliModel: if prefix-before-first-`/` matches a known provider, use it as provider and the rest as pattern.
   - Else try exact full-cliModel match (handles slash-in-id like openrouter `openai/gpt-4o:extended`).
   - If both `--provider` and `--model` given and `cliModel` starts with `provider/`, strip the prefix.
   - Filter candidates by provider if known, then `parseModelPattern(pattern, candidates, .{ .allow_invalid_thinking_level_fallback = false })`.
   - On hit, return {model, thinking_level, warning, error: null}.
   - Inferred-provider fallback (lines 419-439): if we inferred a provider from a slash and got no match within it, retry against ALL models — handles openrouter ids that contain slashes.
   - Provider+pattern with no match: try `buildFallbackModel`. If it returns something, that's a fallback with a warning.
   - Otherwise: error string `Model "<display>" not found. Use --list-models to see available models.`

8. **`findInitialModel(opts) InitialModelResult`** — pi-mono lines 474-554. The hierarchy:
   1. CLI: if `cli_provider AND cli_model`, call `resolveCliModel`. Errors here exit the process with the error string. Hits return immediately.
   2. Scoped models: if `scoped_models.len > 0 AND !is_continuing`, return `scoped_models[0]`. (Phase 2 always passes empty slice; the branch is dead but kept for `--scope` later.)
   3. Settings default: if `default_provider AND default_model_id`, call `registry.find(provider, id)`. Hit → return with `default_thinking_level OR DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL`.
   4. Walk `default_model_per_provider` IN DECLARATION ORDER. For each entry, check `availableModels` (filtered by `hasConfiguredAuth`) for a `(provider, id)` match. First hit wins.
   5. `availableModels[0]` if any exist.
   6. `{ model = null, thinking_level = DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL, fallback_message = null }`.

   `availableModels` here is `registry.getAvailable(arena_alloc)` — note this is the AUTH-FILTERED slice, unlike step 1 of `resolveCliModel`.

9. **`restoreModelFromSession(saved_provider, saved_model_id, current_model, should_print, registry) RestoreResult`** — pi-mono lines 559-628. Used on session resume:
   - Look up `(saved_provider, saved_model_id)` via `registry.find`.
   - If found AND `hasConfiguredAuth` → return restored.
   - Else: `reason = !found ? "model no longer exists" : "no auth configured"`.
   - Fallback chain: if `current_model` non-null, use it. Else walk `default_model_per_provider` against `getAvailable()`. Else `availableModels[0]`. Else null.
   - Returns `{ model, fallback_message }` where `fallback_message` is a human-readable string for the warning.

#### testing

Three tests max:

1. `test "parseModelPattern handles colon-thinking-level suffix"` — pattern `"sonnet:high"` → model claude-sonnet-anything, thinking_level high. pattern `"openai/gpt-4o:extended"` → openrouter model with `:extended` in id, thinking_level null.
2. `test "findInitialModel walks defaults_per_provider in order"` — fake registry with anthropic+openai both authed. Returns anthropic claude-opus-4-6 because it's first in the table.
3. `test "restoreModelFromSession falls back when saved model lacks auth"` — saved=`(anthropic, claude-opus-4-6)`, auth strips anthropic, registry has openai authed. Returns openai's default with a fallback_message.

If you can find pi-mono's `model-resolver.test.ts` golden test cases, port those instead — they're more comprehensive than what I'd hand-write.

### MODIFY: `src/coding_agent.zig` — wire ModelRegistry into AgentSession

Add `model_registry: *ModelRegistry` field. Init in `AgentSession.init` after `auth_storage` is constructed:

```zig
const mr = try allocator.create(model_registry_mod.ModelRegistry);
mr.* = try model_registry_mod.ModelRegistry.init(allocator, auth_storage, &.{});
self.model_registry = mr;
```

`deinit` the registry before destroying the auth storage (registry borrows it).

### MODIFY: `src/main.zig` — delete shim, call findInitialModel

Lines to delete: `resolveModel` (444-475), `default_models_per_provider` const (477-503), `ProviderDefault` struct (478).

Replace the call site (around line 338) with:

```zig
const init_result = resolve.findInitialModel(.{
    .cli_provider = null,  // zi doesn't yet have a --provider flag
    .cli_model = model_arg,
    .scoped_models = &.{},  // --scope not yet wired
    .is_continuing = false,  // resume path is separate
    .default_provider = settings.getDefaultProvider(),
    .default_model_id = settings.getDefaultModel(),
    .default_thinking_level = settings.getDefaultThinkingLevel(),
    .registry = model_registry,
});

const effective_model = init_result.model orelse {
    // print "no model with auth available" error and exit
    return error.NoModelAvailable;
};
```

The hardcoded `claude-sonnet-4` fallback at line 338-353 (the "synthetic Model literal") MUST be deleted. If `findInitialModel` returns null, we exit with a clear message — no silent stub.

### MODIFY: `src/tui/interactive.zig` — bind catalog slice, route lookups

Around line 180 where the existing `auth_storage: *AuthStorage` is stored, add:

```zig
model_catalog: []const protocol.Model,
```

Init it from `ca.model_registry.getAll()` once at TUI startup. Document with a jsdoc comment that this slice's lifetime is bound to AgentSession's ModelRegistry, which outlives Interactive.

Replace lines 1102-1144 (the `switchModelDirect` and the picker code) so they iterate `self.model_catalog` instead of calling `ai_models.getModelById` / `ai_models.findModel`. The `auth_storage.hasAuth(...)` calls already in place STAY — that's the doctrine-sanctioned cross-thread read.

Make sure no TUI code references `ca.model_registry` directly. Use grep to verify.

### MODIFY: session resume path

Find where session resume reconstructs the model. Use:

```bash
rg "savedProvider|saved_provider|restoreModel|model_change" src/session/ src/agent/
```

The resume entry point (likely in `src/session/reader.zig` or wherever `AgentRequest.resume_session` is handled in `interactive.zig`) needs to call `resolve.restoreModelFromSession` instead of raw `getModelById`. Pass it the registry, the saved provider+id, and `should_print=false` (zi's status_text widget handles user-facing messages).

The `fallback_message` (if non-null) becomes a `status_text.setContent(...)` call on the agent thread, then published as a `UiEvent.status_update` to the TUI.

## verification

```bash
zig build                                # MUST be clean
rg "getModelById|findModel\b" src/ \
  --type zig | grep -v ai/model_registry | grep -v ai/models.zig | grep -v ai/resolve
# expected: NO hits — all callers should route through registry or resolve
rg "default_models_per_provider" src/    # expected: NO hits in src/, only in defaults.zig
zig test src/ai/model_registry.zig       # 3 tests pass
zig test src/ai/resolve.zig              # 3 tests pass
```

## acceptance criteria

- [ ] `defaults.zig` exists, references the 4 phase-1 entries, all 4 ids verified to exist in `models_generated.zig`
- [ ] `ModelRegistry` is session-owned, immutable, holds borrowed `*AuthStorage`
- [ ] Bundle (`provider_defaults.zig`) is UNTOUCHED
- [ ] `resolve.zig` ports all 9 functions listed above with line-cited pi-mono comments
- [ ] `main.zig:resolveModel` and `default_models_per_provider` table are DELETED
- [ ] `main.zig` calls `resolve.findInitialModel` and exits cleanly when it returns null
- [ ] TUI binds `model_catalog: []const Model` at init and never calls `ca.model_registry.*`
- [ ] TUI keeps direct `auth_storage.hasAuth()` reads (per oracle finding)
- [ ] Session resume calls `resolve.restoreModelFromSession`
- [ ] `zig build` clean
- [ ] 3 tests in model_registry.zig + 3 tests in resolve.zig pass
- [ ] grep verifies no leftover `getModelById`/`findModel` callers outside the new files

## anti-patterns to refuse

- DO NOT plumb settings into ModelRegistry yet. `custom_models` is `&.{}` for phase 2. Phase 5 wires it.
- DO NOT add a `--provider` CLI flag. zi doesn't have one yet; the resolve.zig signature accepts `cli_provider` for future use, but main.zig passes `null`.
- DO NOT make ModelRegistry mutable or add `register*` methods. Phase 5 will pass custom models at init time.
- DO NOT touch `Bundle` / `provider_defaults.zig`. Different concern, oracle was explicit.
- DO NOT publish a `model_catalog` snapshot through `event_queue`. Direct slice binding at TUI init is sanctioned because the catalog is immutable for the session lifetime in v1. Adding event-queue plumbing for an immutable read is over-engineering and violates simplest-viable-change.
- DO NOT add scope/glob/`--scope` support. `scoped_models` parameter exists but is always empty. Future issue.

# Phase 3 — Register openai-responses + openai-codex-responses + openai-completions providers in Bundle

## context

Read the parent epic first. After phase 2, `ModelRegistry` and `resolve.zig` are in place, so model resolution picks the right `(provider, api, base_url)` tuple for any model the user asks for — but `Bundle.init` (`src/ai/provider_defaults.zig:43-64`) still only registers ONE provider: `anthropic-messages`. Attempting to stream `gpt-5.4` under `.openai_responses` silently no-ops inside `StreamClosure.streamFn` because `Registry.get("openai-responses")` returns null. That's the zi-yjc bug the Bundle was invented to prevent, and phase 3 is where we deliver on that promise.

## scope

3 new provider implementations + Bundle wiring. ~1200 lines of new zig. Deep protocol work — this is where the "don't approximate the protocol" doctrine matters most.

## provider reference: use `anthropic.zig` as the structural template

`src/ai/anthropic.zig` is the existing, working provider. Study it first. Pay attention to:

- How it constructs HTTP requests, headers, and payloads via `std.json.Stringify`
- SSE parsing via `src/ai/sse.zig`
- Event emission through the `AssistantMessageEvent` union — ordering matters, partial state must always be internally consistent
- Allocator discipline — strings in events are backed by arena or msg_allocator per the threading doctrine
- Cancellation threading via `AbortSignal`
- Retry/backoff via `max_retry_delay_ms`

## three new providers

### 1. `src/ai/openai_completions.zig` (~350 lines)

The OpenAI-completions chat format (`POST /chat/completions` with `stream: true`). Used by openrouter and future custom-openai-compatible providers.

**pi-mono reference**: `.references/pi-mono/packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts`. Read it fully before writing. Trace:
- Payload construction (messages, tools, tool_choice, stream_options)
- Role mapping (developer vs system per `compat.supports_developer_role`)
- `reasoning_effort` handling per `compat.reasoning_effort_map` and `compat.supports_reasoning_effort`
- Tool call streaming — tool arg deltas come as string chunks that need concatenation
- `stream_options: { include_usage: true }` gated by `compat.supports_usage_in_streaming`
- `max_tokens` vs `max_completion_tokens` field selection per `compat.max_tokens_field`
- OpenRouter routing preferences injection when `compat.open_router_routing` is set
- Thinking format conversion (openai/openrouter/zai/qwen) when `compat.thinking_format` is set

**register as**: `"openai-completions"` in Bundle.init.

**testing**: one conformance test using a captured SSE fixture from openrouter. One behavior test verifying that a streamed tool call with split-arg-deltas concatenates correctly before emitting `toolcall_end`.

### 2. `src/ai/openai_responses.zig` (~450 lines)

The OpenAI Responses API (`POST /v1/responses` with SSE). Used by `api.openai.com/v1` for GPT-5+ models.

**pi-mono reference**: `.references/pi-mono/packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses.ts`. This is the more complex provider — the Responses API has a different event stream shape than completions:
- `response.output_item.added` / `response.output_item.done` for each output item (reasoning, message, function_call)
- `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` / `.done` for thinking blocks
- `response.output_text.delta` / `.done` for text
- `response.function_call_arguments.delta` for tool calls
- Top-level `response.completed` with usage

Reasoning items carry an opaque encrypted payload in `encrypted_content` — store in `ThinkingContent.thinking_signature`. This matters for phase 4 (codex extends this provider).

**important bits**:
- `store` field gated by `compat.supports_store` — false for codex, true for api.openai.com
- `reasoning_effort` via `reasoning: { effort: ... }` payload field
- Text signature metadata (`TextSignatureV1`) — see `protocol.zig:127-141`
- `response_id` must be captured from `response.created` and set on `AssistantMessage.response_id`

**register as**: `"openai-responses"` in Bundle.init.

**testing**: conformance test using a captured responses API fixture. Verify that reasoning summary text + final answer text come through as separate thinking and text content blocks in the right order.

### 3. `src/ai/openai_codex.zig` (~350 lines, extends openai_responses)

The OpenAI Codex Responses API (`POST /backend-api/codex/responses` at `chatgpt.com`). Uses PKCE oauth tokens instead of api keys.

**pi-mono reference**: `.references/pi-mono/packages/ai/src/providers/openai-codex.ts` or wherever the codex impl lives (grep for `chatgpt.com/backend-api` or `openai-codex-responses`).

**key differences from openai_responses**:
- Base URL: `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api` (from `CODEX_BASE_URL` in phase 1a)
- Endpoint path is NOT `/v1/responses` — trace pi-mono to get the exact path
- Auth header: `Authorization: Bearer <chatgpt_access_token>` where the token comes from `AuthStorage["openai-codex"].access_token` (phase 4 populates this)
- Additional headers pi-mono sets: trace them. Likely includes User-Agent, OpenAI-Beta, etc.
- `store: false` always (responses aren't persisted in the ChatGPT account)
- Token refresh on 401 — phase 4 work. For phase 3, just surface the error.

**strategy**: factor shared logic into `openai_responses_core.zig` that takes an auth-header factory + base_url as parameters, and have both `openai_responses.zig` and `openai_codex.zig` delegate. This avoids copy-paste but keeps the two providers as distinct registry entries.

**register as**: `"openai-codex-responses"` in Bundle.init.

**testing**: one smoke test that constructs the URL and headers correctly given a fake access token. Full integration test deferred to phase 4.

## Bundle.init changes

`src/ai/provider_defaults.zig` — extend the struct and init sequence. Current registers just `anthropic`. Target:

```zig
pub const Bundle = struct {
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    registry: *provider_mod.Registry,

    anthropic_prov: *anthropic.AnthropicProvider,
    openai_responses_prov: *openai_responses.OpenAIResponsesProvider,
    openai_codex_prov: *openai_codex.OpenAICodexProvider,
    openai_completions_prov: *openai_completions.OpenAICompletionsProvider,

    pub fn init(allocator: std.mem.Allocator) !*Bundle {
        // ... existing anthropic init ...

        const oair = try allocator.create(openai_responses.OpenAIResponsesProvider);
        oair.* = openai_responses.OpenAIResponsesProvider.init(allocator);
        try registry.register("openai-responses", oair.provider(), null);

        const oacx = try allocator.create(openai_codex.OpenAICodexProvider);
        oacx.* = openai_codex.OpenAICodexProvider.init(allocator);
        try registry.register("openai-codex-responses", oacx.provider(), null);

        const oac = try allocator.create(openai_completions.OpenAICompletionsProvider);
        oac.* = openai_completions.OpenAICompletionsProvider.init(allocator);
        try registry.register("openai-completions", oac.provider(), null);

        self.* = .{
            .allocator = allocator,
            .registry = registry,
            .anthropic_prov = anth,
            .openai_responses_prov = oair,
            .openai_codex_prov = oacx,
            .openai_completions_prov = oac,
        };
        return self;
    }

    pub fn deinit(self: *Bundle) void {
        self.registry.deinit();
        self.allocator.destroy(self.registry);
        self.allocator.destroy(self.openai_completions_prov);
        self.allocator.destroy(self.openai_codex_prov);
        self.allocator.destroy(self.openai_responses_prov);
        self.allocator.destroy(self.anthropic_prov);
        self.allocator.destroy(self);
    }
};
```

Maintain the `errdefer` discipline from the existing init.

## auth-storage contract for the three new providers

For phase 3, `AuthStorage.getAuth(provider_key)` must return:

- `"openai"` → API key from `auth.json.openai` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` env
- `"openrouter"` → API key from `auth.json.openrouter` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` env
- `"openai-codex"` → **phase 4 placeholder**. For phase 3, return `error.AuthNotConfigured` or similar; phase 4 populates it.

Check `src/auth/storage.zig` to see the existing contract. If the keys aren't already supported, add them in this phase. The provider key strings must match `json_util.providerToString(m.provider)` outputs.

## verification

```bash
zig build                                # clean
# pick a single openrouter model that's free, stream a trivial prompt
./zig-out/bin/zi -p --model "openrouter/auto" "say hi" < /dev/null
# same with openai (requires OPENAI_API_KEY)
./zig-out/bin/zi -p --model "gpt-5.4" "say hi" < /dev/null
# verify codex fails gracefully (no auth) until phase 4
./zig-out/bin/zi -p --model "openai-codex/gpt-5.4" "say hi" < /dev/null
# expected: clean error mentioning codex auth not configured, not a silent hang
```

## acceptance criteria

- [ ] `openai_responses.zig` streams from `api.openai.com/v1/responses` with full event-order parity vs pi-mono
- [ ] `openai_codex.zig` constructs correct URL + headers for codex endpoint (streaming deferred to phase 4 integration)
- [ ] `openai_completions.zig` streams from openrouter successfully
- [ ] Shared logic factored into a common helper file, no copy-paste of event parsing between `openai_responses` and `openai_codex`
- [ ] All three registered in `Bundle.init` with correct api strings
- [ ] `Bundle.deinit` tears down in reverse order, no leaks
- [ ] `zig build` clean
- [ ] Smoke test: `zi -p --model openrouter/auto "hi"` actually returns a response
- [ ] Smoke test: `zi -p --model gpt-5.4 "hi"` returns a response when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set
- [ ] Codex provider returns a clear auth error, not a silent no-op, when invoked without phase 4 auth
- [ ] `compat` field on Model is honored where pi-mono honors it (supports_developer_role, reasoning_effort_map, open_router_routing)

## anti-patterns to refuse

- DO NOT copy-paste openai_responses into openai_codex. Factor shared logic.
- DO NOT hand-roll JSON. Use `std.json.Stringify` for writing, `std.json.parseFromSlice` for reading (see `src/session/json.zig` for the pattern).
- DO NOT skip the compat field. If `compat.supports_developer_role == false`, send `"system"` not `"developer"`. Trace pi-mono for every compat branch.
- DO NOT add new custom headers to the Model struct. Use the existing `headers: ?[]const Header` field.
- DO NOT try to implement codex PKCE oauth in this phase. That's phase 4. Phase 3 only reads a pre-populated token from AuthStorage and fails cleanly if absent.

description:
# Phase 5 — Custom models via ~/.config/.zi/settings.json models[]

## context

Read the parent epic first. This is the fireworks-kimi use case: a user wants to point zi at a model served by an openai-compatible provider that isn't in the built-in catalog, without writing zig or a lua extension. The mechanism: a `models: []` array in `settings.json` that gets merged into `ModelRegistry` at session init.

This phase ONLY depends on phase 2 (the ModelRegistry seam). It does NOT depend on phase 3/4 because custom models reuse already-registered apis. If a user defines a custom model with `api: "anthropic-messages"`, it streams through phase 3's anthropic provider. If `api: "openai-completions"`, phase 3's openai_completions. No new provider implementations needed.

## scope

~120 lines across `src/settings/types.zig`, `src/settings/json.zig`, `src/coding_agent.zig`. Trivial compared to phases 2-4.

## settings schema

Add to `Settings` in `src/settings/types.zig`:

```zig
pub const CustomModel = struct {
    id: []const u8,
    name: []const u8,
    /// Must be one of the registered Api strings (anthropic-messages,
    /// openai-responses, openai-completions, openai-codex-responses).
    /// Custom api values are rejected at load time because there's no
    /// provider to stream them.
    api: protocol.Api,
    /// Custom provider name, stored as .custom variant on the Provider union.
    /// This keeps it distinct from built-in providers for auth lookup.
    /// Example: "fireworks-kimi" → auth.json["fireworks-kimi"] = "<api_key>"
    provider: []const u8,
    base_url: []const u8,
    reasoning: bool = false,
    input_has_image: bool = false,
    cost: protocol.Model.Cost = .{ .input = 0, .output = 0, .cache_read = 0, .cache_write = 0 },
    context_window: u64 = 4096,
    max_tokens: u64 = 4096,
    headers: ?[]const protocol.Header = null,
    compat: ?protocol.Compat = null,
};

pub const Settings = struct {
    // ... existing fields ...
    models: []const CustomModel = &.{},
};
```

## JSON shape in settings.json

```json
{
  "defaultProvider": "fireworks-kimi",
  "defaultModel": "kimi-k2.5",
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "kimi-k2.5",
      "name": "Kimi K2.5 (Fireworks)",
      "api": "openai-completions",
      "provider": "fireworks-kimi",
      "baseUrl": "https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1",
      "reasoning": true,
      "inputHasImage": false,
      "cost": { "input": 0.6, "output": 2.5, "cacheRead": 0.06, "cacheWrite": 0 },
      "contextWindow": 131072,
      "maxTokens": 8192,
      "headers": [{ "key": "X-Fireworks-Account", "value": "..." }],
      "compat": {
        "openaiCompletions": {
          "supportsDeveloperRole": false,
          "maxTokensField": "maxCompletionTokens"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

camelCase wire, snake_case zig fields — follow `src/settings/json.zig` conventions. Use `std.json.parseFromSlice` into the struct directly if feasible.

## merging into ModelRegistry

`src/coding_agent.zig:AgentSession.init` currently passes `&.{}` for `custom_models` (phase 2 placeholder). Change to:

```zig
const custom = try convertSettingsModels(allocator, settings.models);
defer allocator.free(custom);

const mr = try allocator.create(ModelRegistry);
mr.* = try ModelRegistry.init(allocator, auth_storage, custom);
```

`convertSettingsModels` translates `[]const CustomModel` → `[]protocol.Model` with the provider wrapped as `.{ .custom = name }`. Validation:

1. `api` string must resolve via `parseApi` to one of the four registered apis (`anthropic_messages`, `openai_responses`, `openai_completions`, `openai_codex_responses`). Reject others at load time with a clear error naming the bad model.
2. `provider` string must NOT collide with a built-in provider name (`anthropic`, `openai`, `openai_codex`, `openrouter`). This prevents accidental shadowing. Reject with clear error.
3. `base_url` must be a non-empty string starting with `http://` or `https://`.
4. `id` must be non-empty and unique within the custom list.

Failed validation at init time: print errors to stderr, exit 1 (don't silently drop bad entries — that's the drift we're trying to avoid).

## auth for custom providers

The provider name in `settings.json.models[i].provider` (e.g. `"fireworks-kimi"`) becomes the key in `auth.json`. `AuthStorage.hasAuth("fireworks-kimi")` checks:

1. `auth.json["fireworks-kimi"]` — direct api key
2. Env var `FIREWORKS_KIMI_API_KEY` (or similar normalization — check what pi-mono does)

No code change in AuthStorage if it already supports arbitrary string keys (it should — check). If it hardcodes a known-keys list, remove that restriction.

## registry invariant

`ModelRegistry.init` with custom_models non-empty:

1. Allocate `custom_backing = allocator.alloc(Model, builtin.len + custom.len)`
2. Copy `generated.models` into `custom_backing[0..builtin.len]`
3. Copy converted custom models into `custom_backing[builtin.len..]`
4. Set `models = custom_backing`
5. `deinit` frees `custom_backing`

**Collision policy**: if a custom model has `(provider = .{.custom="x"}, id = "y")` and there's no built-in `(provider=.{.custom="x"}, id="y")` (impossible since customs always use `.custom` variant and built-ins don't), there's no collision risk. Two custom models with the same `(provider, id)` are rejected at validation (step 4 above).

## verification

```bash
zig build

# create a test settings file
cat > /tmp/zi-test/.zi/settings.json <<EOF
{
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "kimi-k2.5",
      "name": "Kimi K2.5",
      "api": "openai-completions",
      "provider": "fireworks-kimi",
      "baseUrl": "https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1",
      "contextWindow": 131072,
      "maxTokens": 8192
    }
  ]
}
EOF

cd /tmp/zi-test
export FIREWORKS_KIMI_API_KEY=fake
./zig-out/bin/zi --model "fireworks-kimi/kimi-k2.5" --list-models 2>&1 | grep fireworks-kimi
# expected: the custom model appears in the list

# bad api rejection
jq '.models[0].api = "fake-api"' /tmp/zi-test/.zi/settings.json > /tmp/a && mv /tmp/a /tmp/zi-test/.zi/settings.json
./zig-out/bin/zi 2>&1
# expected: clear error "settings.models[0] has unknown api 'fake-api'"

# provider shadowing rejection
jq '.models[0].provider = "openai"' /tmp/zi-test/.zi/settings.json > /tmp/a && mv /tmp/a /tmp/zi-test/.zi/settings.json
./zig-out/bin/zi 2>&1
# expected: clear error "settings.models[0].provider 'openai' shadows a built-in provider"
```

## acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CustomModel` struct in `settings/types.zig` with camelCase JSON mapping
- [ ] `Settings.models: []const CustomModel` field with `[]` default
- [ ] JSON load + save round-trip for a settings file with 2 custom models
- [ ] Validation at load time: bad api string, provider shadowing, bad base_url, duplicate ids — all rejected with clear errors
- [ ] `AgentSession.init` converts and passes custom models to `ModelRegistry.init`
- [ ] `ModelRegistry.custom_backing` is owned and freed on deinit
- [ ] Custom models appear in `resolve.findInitialModel`'s availableModels when their provider has auth
- [ ] A custom model with `api = "openai-completions"` and a valid base_url streams successfully using phase 3's provider (no new zig code needed)
- [ ] `zi --list-models` (if it exists) shows custom models mixed in
- [ ] `AuthStorage.hasAuth("<custom-provider-name>")` works for arbitrary strings
- [ ] 2 tests: JSON round-trip, validation rejections

## anti-patterns to refuse

- DO NOT add custom model support by making `ModelRegistry` mutable post-init. Pass customs at construction, period.
- DO NOT silently drop invalid entries. Reject at load time with errors naming the bad field.
- DO NOT allow custom models to use the `.custom` Api variant. All four allowed apis must be one of the built-in enum variants, because those are the only ones Bundle registers.
- DO NOT allow custom provider names that match built-in providers. Shadowing is a bug, not a feature.
- DO NOT invent new auth-storage features for custom providers. If AuthStorage already accepts arbitrary string keys (it should), use what's there.
- DO NOT couple phase 5 to phase 4 (codex). Custom codex-pathway models are nonsense — codex is a specific subscription, not a configurable api.

title: fix: --tools CLI flag must be a strict allowlist (prevent Task-in-Task recursion)
description:
## problem

`zig build test` currently fork-bombs: a Task tool test fixture spawns `zi --mode json -p --no-session --tools bash,read,grep,find Task: ...` as a subprocess, and that subprocess *also* registers the Task tool unconditionally. The spawned zi then invokes Task again → recursive spawn → hundreds of zi processes before the OS kills the parent.

Discovered while landing zi-1er.3 phase 3b (openai-responses provider) — blocks `zig build test` entirely. Reproduces without any phase 3b code (verified by reverting `ai/root.zig` inclusion and re-running).

## root cause

zi's `--tools` CLI flag is not honored as a strict allowlist. The spawned process receives `--tools bash,read,grep,find` but still registers Task on top of those four. pi-mono handles this correctly — see `.references/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:266`:

```ts
if (agent.tools && agent.tools.length > 0) args.push("--tools", agent.tools.join(","));
```

pi-mono's subagent example sets an explicit tool allowlist per subagent (via frontmatter) and relies on the parent process honoring `--tools` as a filter. zi must match that contract.

## fix

In zi's main.zig CLI parser: when `--tools` is present, the registered toolset must be EXACTLY the intersection of the requested list with the available set. Tools not in the list must not be registered — including Task, which is currently always-on.

Acceptance:
- `zi --tools bash` registers bash only (no Task, no read, no grep, no find, no edit, no write).
- `zig build test` no longer fork-bombs (Task subagent test spawns a child that registers a reduced toolset without Task).
- Existing invocations without `--tools` keep the full toolset.

## context

- Discovered in phase 3b of zi-1er.3 — see commit 1a9584b for the encounter.
- pi-mono reference: `.references/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/subagent/`
- Blocks the `zig build test` gate from being usable as the combined build+test check documented in AGENTS.md.
close_reason: Shipped in 79aef9e. Fork-bomb premise was wrong — direct test binary runs 342 tests to completion in ~30s with no spawns. The --tools strict-allowlist fix still lands on its own merits (pi-mono parity + superset: zi can whitelist ext tools like Task where pi-mono is builtin-only). Real cause of 'zig build test' hang is ziglang/zig#15091 — filed separately.

title: feat(ai): TextSignatureV1.phase round-trip on inbound assistant messages in openai_responses
description:
## problem

In phase 3b, `openai_responses_core.writeAssistantMessage` parses `text_signature` (TextSignatureV1 JSON) for the message `id` but drops the `phase` field. The current code has a commented-out phase-extraction block with a lifetime hazard: `parsed.value.object.get("phase").string` borrows from a `std.json.ParseResult` arena that's freed by `defer parsed.deinit()` before `jw.write(phase)` runs.

Fix is straightforward: `allocator.dupe(u8, ...)` the phase string out of the parser arena, track it alongside `msg_id_alloc`, free it via the same deferred cleanup. Then emit `phase: "commentary" | "final_answer"` on the outbound message object.

## why this matters (eventually)

OpenAI's multi-phase prompting (commentary vs. final_answer passes) relies on phase round-trip to pair outputs across turns. Without it, zi loses the distinction between a reasoning-style commentary pass and the user-facing answer on multi-turn sessions against gpt-5.4. Phase 3b sessions work fine in single-turn; the gap shows up in multi-turn conversations with phased reasoning.

## scope

- Dup phase out of the parser arena in `openai_responses_core.writeAssistantMessage`
- Emit `phase` field on the function_call's parent message object when present
- Add one fixture test: assistant message with `text_signature` containing `{v:1,id:"msg_x",phase:"commentary"}` → serialized output contains `"phase":"commentary"`

## references

- `src/ai/openai_responses_core.zig` writeAssistantMessage comment block (marks the deferral)
- pi-mono: `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts:179-192` (outbound phase handling)

title: Overlay system — handle-based, cell-buffer composited
description:
Add overlay stack to Interactive with handle-based lifecycle and cell-buffer compositing.

## Problem
pi-mono has TUI.showOverlay with rich OverlayOptions + OverlayHandle. zi has no overlay system. Blocks extension custom UIs, future model/session selectors.

## Design (oracle-reviewed)
Overlay stack on Interactive:

    const OverlayEntry = struct {
        id: u64,
        component: Component,
        options: OverlayOptions,
        pre_focus: ?Component,
        hidden: bool,
        non_capturing: bool,
        focus_order: u64,
    };

OverlayOptions (parity with pi-mono):
- width/minWidth/maxHeight (absolute or percentage)
- anchor (center, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, etc)
- offsetX/offsetY, row/col
- margin (per-side or uniform)
- visible fn(w,h)→bool for dynamic visibility
- nonCapturing flag

OverlayHandle methods:
- hide() — permanent remove
- setHidden(bool) — temporary toggle
- focus()/unfocus()
- isFocused()/isHidden()

## Rendering (zi-specific advantage)
Cell-buffer compositing: render root tree into buffer first, then render each visible overlay into sub-region on top. Simpler than pi-mono's line-splice approach.

## Focus rules
- Show: save preFocus, setFocus(overlay) unless nonCapturing
- Hide: focus topmost visible capturing overlay, or restore preFocus
- Invisible overlay (terminal resize): redirect focus

## Depends on
- F (focus model) — overlay focus save/restore uses FocusManager

- contract: docs/extension-ui-contract.md section H

title: feat(ai): foreign tool-call-id fc_<hash> normalization for cross-provider history
description:
## problem

When a session is resumed across providers (e.g. assistant turn N was served by anthropic-messages, turn N+1 switches to openai-responses), the openai-responses API requires all function_call item ids to match the `fc_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}` shape. Pi-mono normalizes foreign ids via `buildForeignResponsesItemId`:

```ts
const buildForeignResponsesItemId = (itemId: string): string => {
    const normalized = `fc_${shortHash(itemId)}`;
    return normalized.length > 64 ? normalized.slice(0, 64) : normalized;
};
```

See `.references/pi-mono/packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts:100-117` — pi-mono routes foreign-provider tool calls through this normalizer, stable-hashing the original id so that within a single turn multiple references to the same logical tool call resolve to the same `fc_xxx`.

zi's phase 3b port skipped this: tool call ids are passed through verbatim. This is fine as long as zi stays within one provider per session (today's default), but breaks as soon as a session mid-flight switches from, say, anthropic's `toolu_01ABC` to openai-responses.

## scope

1. Port `shortHash` utility (or implement via std.hash.Wyhash + base62) into `src/ai/json_util.zig` or a new `hash_util.zig`
2. In `openai_responses_core.writeAssistantMessage` + the tool_result writer, detect foreign ids (anything not matching `fc_.*` or lacking the `|` composite form) and normalize via `buildForeignResponsesItemId`
3. Mirror pi-mono's `normalizeToolCallId` helper — the first part (call_id) uses a looser sanitizer, the second part (item_id) requires the `fc_` prefix
4. Conformance test: an assistant message with a synthetic anthropic `toolu_xxx` id serializes to an openai-responses `function_call` with `id = fc_<stable-hash>`

## references

- `.references/pi-mono/packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts:86-117`
- `.references/pi-mono/packages/ai/src/utils/hash.ts` (shortHash)

title: feat(ai): plumb reasoning_effort / reasoning_summary through StreamOptions
description:
## problem

zi's providers (anthropic, openai_completions, openai_responses) all currently drop the caller's reasoning level on the floor. `SimpleStreamOptions.reasoning` is parsed and stored but never reaches the provider payload:

- anthropic: no `thinking.type=enabled` + `thinking.budget_tokens`
- openai_completions: no `reasoning_effort` field
- openai_responses (phase 3b): defaults to `reasoning: { effort: "none" }` — matches pi-mono's unset-options fallback but means reasoning models never actually reason

This is OK for phase 3a (no registered reasoning models yet) and phase 3b (no live smoke test), but it becomes a visible gap as soon as phase 3c registers gpt-5.4 via the openai-codex provider and users try `/think high`.

## scope

Wire `StreamOptions.reasoning_level` (new field) through all three providers in one coordinated change:

1. Add `reasoning_level: ?ThinkingLevel = null` to `protocol.StreamOptions` (pi-mono parity: `reasoningEffort` on provider options).
2. Build per-provider payload fields from it:
   - **anthropic**: `thinking: { type: "enabled", budget_tokens: <budget from ThinkingBudgets> }`. Match pi-mono's `anthropic.ts` budget mapping.
   - **openai_completions**: `reasoning_effort: <minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh>`, gated by model reasoning flag.
   - **openai_responses**: `reasoning: { effort, summary: "auto" }` + `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`. Stop defaulting to `effort: "none"`.
3. Wire `SimpleStreamOptions.reasoning` + `thinking_budgets` → `StreamOptions.reasoning_level` in each provider's `streamSimpleImplWrapper`.
4. Integration test: a live call against each of the three registered apis with `/think high` produces a thinking block (or a non-empty reasoning signature for anthropic).

title: editor slash-command top-pick tests expect /resume but get /reload
description:
## symptom

5 test failures in `src/tui/components/editor.zig` when running the test binary directly (`zig build test` hangs separately — see zi-x25).

```
FAIL: slash command Tab accepts top pick without submitting
  expected: '/resume '
  actual:   '/reload '

FAIL: slash command Enter on partial text accepts top pick and submits
  expected: '/resume ⏎'
  actual:   '/reload ⏎'
```

(3 more with the same signature — all asserting the fuzzy-match top pick is `/resume` when it's actually `/reload`.)

## likely cause

a slash command was added (`/reload`) that now sorts above `/resume` for whatever empty-or-short query the tests use. fuzzy.zig uses alphabetical tiebreaker for empty queries, and 'reload' < 'resume' alphabetically — so if the test fires Tab on an empty editor, `/reload` legitimately wins.

either:
- the tests need updating to match the new top pick
- the fuzzy ranking for the test query changed and the old top is no longer #1
- `/reload` shouldn't be in the autocomplete list at all for this context

## fix

1. read the failing tests in `src/tui/components/editor.zig` around line 875 and 918
2. check what query they fire against and what the expected picker order is
3. update the expectations OR fix whatever changed the ranking

## context

discovered while validating the zi-1ry `--tools` fix (79aef9e) — the direct test binary run exposed these failures after `zig build test` was found to deadlock on an unrelated upstream zig bug.

title: zig build test hangs on server protocol deadlock (ziglang/zig#15091)
description:
## symptom

`zig build test` hangs indefinitely. direct run of the test binary (`.zig-cache/o/<hash>/test`) completes all 342 tests in ~30s without issue.

## stack traces (taken while hung)

```
test pid: main → test_runner.mainServer → Server.receiveMessage
           → Reader.fill → posix.readv  (blocked on stdin)

build pid: main → runStepNames → WaitGroup.wait
           → Futex.wait  (blocked on test completion)
```

## root cause

ziglang/zig#15091 — 'prevent confusing debugging experience when users write garbage to stdout, interfering with the build runner / test runner protocol'. open since 2023, urgent milestone, not fixed.

when any test (or code under test) writes to stdout, it corrupts the zig test runner's outbound binary protocol stream. build reads garbage as an InMessage header, can't parse it, deadlocks. test waits for the next-request message that never comes.

lua linkage (vendored C static lib) is NOT the cause — that's a different bug (ben-krieger gist, zig 0.16-dev.2040) that *panics* with `error.EndOfStream` instead of hanging. ours hangs → #15091 signature.

## blocks

- `zig build test` as a CI / pre-push gate
- catching regressions from phase 3b openai-responses port and future phases
- AGENTS.md already warns 'do NOT run `zig build test` — it times out' — this is the ticket to fix that
